steps.text: [Energy and Trucking Data Researcher]: Fetch the EIA Midwest diesel series and save the raw data
steps.do: 1) Use fetch_url on the EIA API v2 URL for series EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG (DEMO_KEY, weekly, sorted by period descending, length 60). If that fails, use the dnav history page https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMD_EPD2D_PTE_R20_DPG&f=W. 2) Read the whole response. Write the 60 newest week/price pairs to raw_eia.txt with the Write tool, passing the path explicitly. 3) Note the URL, today's retrieval date and the newest week seen. Do not fabricate any value.
steps.output: raw_eia.txt with at least 52 week/price pairs, plus a note giving the URL, retrieval date and newest week
steps.done_when: raw_eia.txt exists and holds at least 52 dated weekly prices copied from the fetched EIA response, or the failure is explained.

steps.text: [Energy and Trucking Data Researcher]: Find the latest ATRI marginal cost per mile and fuel share
steps.do: 1) Search for the latest ATRI 'An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking' report. 2) Fetch the ATRI page or press release and extract the title, release date, cost data year, total marginal cost per mile and fuel cost per mile. 3) Compute the fuel share = fuel / total. 4) If a figure is paywalled or missing, say NOT FOUND and give a documented substitute (such as the prior-year report) with its source. 5) State whether the full report or a summary was used.
steps.output: list: ATRI figures (report title, release date, cost data year, total $/mile, fuel $/mile, fuel share) each with URL and date, and flags for anything not found
steps.done_when: The list gives report title, release date and cost data year; it gives total and fuel cost per mile with a computed fuel share; every figure has a URL and a date; any missing figure is labelled NOT FOUND with its substitute; it says whether the full report or a summary was used.

steps.text: [Fuel Cost and Surcharge Modeler]: Build workbook core sheets: Inputs, Weekly, Bands
steps.do: 1) Read weekly_prices.csv. 2) Create fuel_surcharge_workbook.xlsx. Inputs sheet: 35, 2300, 6.2, 1.25 as the only hard-coded parameters, derived weekly miles and gallons as formulas, and assumption notes (constant gallons, midpoint band convention, surcharge on every mile, Class 8 = GVWR over 33,000 lb). 3) Weekly: 52 rows with surcharge =ROUND((price-base)/mpg,2), gallons from Inputs, fleet cost = price*gallons, fuel $/mi = price/mpg, Source. 4) Bands: 40 rows from $3.00 to $5.00 with low, high, midpoint and surcharge formula.
steps.output: table: workbook sheet map (sheet x key columns x formula used) and the file fuel_surcharge_workbook.xlsx
steps.done_when: fuel_surcharge_workbook.xlsx exists; Weekly has 52 data rows whose surcharge, gallons, fleet cost and fuel $/mi cells are formulas; Bands has 40 formula rows; Inputs holds the four parameters and the written assumption notes.

steps.text: [Fuel Cost and Surcharge Modeler]: Add Summary and Sources sheets to the workbook
steps.do: 1) Open the workbook from step 3. 2) Summary: formulas for average price, highest and lowest week (INDEX/MATCH), 52-week total fuel cost, average fuel cost per mile, ATRI total, fuel per mile and fuel share (inputs marked with source and date) and the carrier-minus-ATRI fuel per mile gap. 3) Sources: series ID, URLs, retrieval dates, ATRI report title, release date, cost data year, period and scope caveat, and the proxy statement. 4) Mark any ATRI substitute.
steps.output: table: Summary sheet map (metric x formula x cell) and the updated fuel_surcharge_workbook.xlsx
steps.done_when: The workbook has Summary with formulas for average, highest week, lowest week, total, average $/mi and the ATRI gap; ATRI inputs show source and date; Sources lists series ID, URLs, retrieval dates, ATRI details and the proxy statement; any ATRI substitute is marked.

steps.text: [Fuel Cost and Surcharge Modeler]: Compute Decimal statistics and draw the chart
steps.do: 1) In Python, recompute every weekly surcharge, fleet cost and the stats with Decimal ROUND_HALF_UP, mirroring the workbook. 2) Print the stats table (mean, highest and lowest week with dates, total cost, average $/mi, ATRI fuel $/mi and gap) and the 40-band table. 3) Draw the dual-axis PNG chart (price left, surcharge right) with title, legend, source note and caption.
steps.output: table: stats summary and the 40-band surcharge table, plus the file price_surcharge_chart.png
steps.done_when: price_surcharge_chart.png exists at least 1200 px wide with 52 points on each line, titled axes and a legend; the stats table (average, highest and lowest week with dates, total, average $/mi, ATRI gap) is printed; the 40-band table is printed; the Decimal values are stated to mirror the workbook formulas.

steps.text: [Independent Data and Model Verifier]: Verify EIA prices and ATRI figures
steps.do: 1) Check weekly_prices.csv: 52 rows, 7-day spacing, plausible range, series ID. 2) Re-fetch at least 3 EIA weeks (first, a middle one, last) and compare; confirm the latest week is the newest EIA release. 3) Check the ATRI figures, title, release date and cost data year against the cited URL, and recompute the fuel share. 4) Check that every figure has a source and a date and that the proxy and substitutes are flagged. 5) Issue a verdict with exact corrections.
steps.output: memo: data verification report with a verdict (PASS / PASS WITH FIXES / FAIL), a table of checks (expected vs actual) and a list of required corrections
steps.done_when: An explicit verdict is stated; the table shows at least 3 re-fetched EIA weeks with expected vs actual, plus the 52-week and spacing checks; the ATRI figures and the fuel share arithmetic are checked against the source; every figure is confirmed to have a citation and a date, with the proxy flagged; each mismatch has a correction.

steps.text: [Independent Data and Model Verifier]: Verify workbook formulas, statistics and chart
steps.do: 1) Open the workbook with openpyxl (formula text, not cached values): confirm formulas in Weekly, Bands and Summary and that Inputs holds the only hard-coded parameters. 2) Parse the formulas and independently recompute all 52 weekly rows (surcharge, gallons, fleet cost, fuel $/mi), the 40 band surcharges and the Summary stats with Decimal half-up. 3) Compare with the modeler's stats table. 4) Check the PNG width, 52 points per line, axis titles and legend. 5) Issue a verdict with exact corrections.
steps.output: memo: workbook and chart verification report with a verdict (PASS / PASS WITH FIXES / FAIL), a table of checks (expected vs actual) and a list of required corrections
steps.done_when: An explicit verdict is stated; the spreadsheet formulas are evaluated independently (all 52 weekly rows, 40 bands and the Summary stats recomputed with Decimal half-up) with mismatches listed; Inputs is confirmed as the only home of hard-coded parameters, with the assumptions written down; the modeler's stats table is compared with the recomputation; the PNG width, point count, axis titles and legend are checked.

steps.text: [Memo Author (Word)]: Write the two-page Word memo
steps.do: 1) Apply the verifiers' corrections. 2) Write the memo sections: bottom line, data and method with assumptions, 40-band multi-column schedule, 52-week results, ATRI comparison with caveat, Not obtained / substituted, Sources with dates. 3) Build the docx with python-docx and narrow margins. 4) Check the page count and trim to at most 2 pages.
steps.output: memo: fuel_surcharge_memo.docx (at most 2 pages) with band table, stats, ATRI comparison, limitations and sources, and the reported page count
steps.done_when: The docx exists and is at most 2 pages; it has a 40-band table from $3.00 to $5.00 in 5-cent steps; average, highest and lowest week appear with dates; the ATRI comparison states report title, release date, cost data year and the period and scope caveat; each figure has a source and date; the proxy, the assumptions and any substitute are stated.

steps.text: [Independent Data and Model Verifier]: Verify the memo against the verified numbers
steps.do: 1) Open the docx and compare every figure with the verified stats and band table. 2) Check the 40 bands against the recomputed Decimal values. 3) Check the page count independently (soffice and pypdf if present, otherwise a conservative estimate). 4) Check that every figure has a source and a date, and that the proxy, assumptions and substitutes are stated. 5) Issue a verdict with exact corrections.
steps.output: memo: memo verification report with a verdict (PASS / PASS WITH FIXES / FAIL), a table of checks (expected vs actual) and required corrections
steps.done_when: An explicit verdict is stated; the memo's key figures and all 40 bands are compared with the verified values; the page count is stated; citations and dates for each figure are confirmed; the proxy, assumptions, ATRI caveat and substitutes are confirmed present; each mismatch has a correction.

steps.do: 1) Open with the exact mandated interpretation line. 2) Summarise the key figures with source and date. 3) List the delivered files (xlsx, png, docx) and the memo page count. 4) State all three verifier verdicts and the limitations, including the proxy, the ATRI period and scope mismatch, and any substitute.
steps.output: memo: final answer with the opening line, results summary, files delivered and limitations
steps.done_when: The answer starts with the mandated line; it lists the three files and the memo page count; it gives all three verdicts; it has a Limitations section with the proxy, the ATRI mismatch and any missing figure and its substitute.

steps.text: [Energy and Trucking Data Researcher]: Build weekly_prices.csv from the saved raw data
steps.do: 1) Read raw_eia.txt with local:Read, giving the path. 2) Take the 52 latest weeks and check they are 7 days apart and that the newest is the latest EIA release. 3) Write weekly_prices.csv with the Write tool, columns week_ending, price_usd_per_gal, series_id, source_url, retrieved_date, 52 rows. 4) In the reply give the retrieval date next to each web figure, name the series, and note that EIA has no Indiana-only series, so Midwest (PADD 2) is the proxy.
steps.output: table: weekly_prices.csv (week_ending x price_usd_per_gal x series_id x source_url x retrieved_date), 52 rows, plus a dated note on the latest week and the series name
steps.done_when: weekly_prices.csv exists with 52 consecutive weekly rows, each with date, price, series ID, source URL and retrieved_date, and the note states the retrieval date and the Midwest proxy.
